Environment Variables live outside of the Python interpreter's scope, they are available to the system. 

In the terminal we create them with `export` and then view them with `echo`.

In python we use `os` and `.getenv()`

::: {.callout-tip}
Second arg to `os.getenv()` is the default value, i.e. if environment variable not set return this value.
:::

As all environment variables are handled outside of Python, they are strings - so that other programs can handle them. Applications/programs need to take care of any type conversion.

Nothing else of note, really.
